choice_d.text: Some of the subjects who were given placebos consumed foods during the study that are naturally rich in vitamin C.

notes_d.body: The placebo group was eating vitamin C-rich foods? If anything, that helps the argument. If both groups were getting vitamin C (one through pills, one through diet) and there was no difference, that is more evidence vitamin C does not help with acne. This answer accidentally supports the conclusion instead of weakening it.

rows.prompt: Which one of the following, if true, most seriously weakens the argument?
rows.stimulus: To test the claim that vitamin C is effective in treating acne, scientists administered it to one group of subjects and a placebo to a control group. The group receiving vitamin C had less severe acne during the study than did the control group. It was subsequently discovered, however, that half of the subjects in each group knew which kind of pill they were given. Among those who could not tell, no difference in the severity of acne was found between the two groups. Therefore, we can tentatively conclude that vitamin C has no real benefit in reducing the severity of acne.

choice_d.text: Some of the subjects who were given placebos consumed foods during the study that are naturally rich in vitamin C.

notes_d.body: If the placebo group also got vitamin C through food, the lack of difference between groups still suggests the pills added no benefit. This supports the conclusion rather than weakening it.

choice_d.text: Some of the subjects who were given placebos consumed foods during the study that are naturally rich in vitamin C.

notes_d.body: D is the most tempting trap. If placebo subjects got vitamin C from food, the control group was not vitamin-free. But D says only that "Some" placebo subjects ate vitamin C-rich foods, which is an ordinary diet and could just as easily describe the vitamin C group. Nothing suggests the food matched the pill's dose or that it happened among the blind subjects. So D barely dents the comparison, while A gives direct evidence that the vitamin helped.
